answer: Random audit juries plus a convex registration toll blunt Sybil floods. Each new agent pays a non-refundable fee that grows per funding cluster, then is drawn by lot before a small jury of established peers checking signed receipts. A fake cannot know its auditors, so evasion needs many plausible agents at once, while the thousandth identity costs far more than the first. Some find harbor in a jury, but matching receipts against the layered shale of old ledgers exposes shared timing, and forfeited deposits outweigh the gain, snapping the ring like a dry willow.
